_comment: Event system. Every event MUST declare a mitigation hook the player controls — enforced by validateEventCatalog() in src/engine/events/events.ts. Mitigation reduces risk but NEVER eliminates it (floorProbability), and mitigation buildings carry ongoing upkeep (data/buildings.json), so 'buy total safety once' is impossible.

_categories.prosperity: Exposure GROWS with success (population, buildings, wealth). These are the anti-snowball levers — thriving draws more risk, so success creates new pressure instead of removing it.
_categories.condition: Exposure is driven by the player's own bad state (unrest, grain shortfall). These compound existing problems rather than rolling independently — a well-run principality rarely sees them.

telegraph.unmitigated: Plague sweeps the villages — no hospital to contain it
telegraph.mitigated: Plague reaches the principality, but the hospital limits the toll

telegraph.unmitigated: Fire tears through the workshops — no wells or firebreaks
telegraph.mitigated: Fire breaks out, but the wells keep it from spreading far

telegraph.unmitigated: Bandits plunder the trade roads — no garrison to patrol them
telegraph.mitigated: Bandits raid the roads, but the garrison drives them off with light losses

telegraph.unmitigated: The peasants rise in revolt — years of grievance boil over
telegraph.mitigated: Unrest erupts into revolt, but the garrison restores order quickly

telegraph.unmitigated: The dry year scorches the fields and empties the barns — no wells to draw on
telegraph.mitigated: The dry year bites, but the wells keep enough water flowing to save most of the stores

telegraph.unmitigated: The heavy rains overwhelm the fields — no dikes to hold the water back
telegraph.mitigated: The rains swell the rivers, but the dikes hold most of the fields dry

telegraph.unmitigated: Famine follows the shortage — the granaries stand empty
telegraph.mitigated: Shortage bites, but granary reserves blunt the famine
